Package ui11.layout.multichild

Class LinearLayout

java.lang.Object
ui11.Widget
ui11.SubstitutedWidget
ui11.layout.multichild.LinearLayout
All Implemented Interfaces:
Cloneable
public final class LinearLayout extends SubstitutedWidget
A layout container, which arranges its children next to each other in horizontal or vertical direction. The available space will be filled by the children, without overlapping each other. No space will remain unused if no gap, justification other than LinearLayout.JustifyContent.STRETCH or child alignment other than LinearLayout.AlignChildren.STRETCH is set, so if the container is forced to stretch, then the children will also grow.

By default, the free space will be distributed equally to all children. This can be overridden using expanded(Widget) which specifies one child to receive all the remaining space, or using withWeight(double, Widget) which specifies a proportion that that dictates what amount of the available space inside the container the item should take up. For example, if one of the children has weight set to 2 while each other has weight set to 1, then that widget would take up twice as much of the distributable space as either one of the others.

A LinearLayout has a main axis and a cross axis. The main axis is the primary axis along which flex items are laid out. The cross axis is the axis perpendicular to the main axis is called the cross axis.

If a LinearLayout has zero children, it behaves the same as an Empty widget instead.

For similar alternatives in other environments, see Flexbox in CSS and Row/Column/Flex in Flutter.

    • withMainAxis

      public static @NonNull LinearLayout.Builder withMainAxis(@NonNull Axis mainAxis)
      Returns a LinearLayout.Builder that can be used to create a layout container that places the specified widgets side by side along the specified axis. If mainAxis is Axis.VERTICAL the container will be a column, if mainAxis is Axis.HORIZONTAL the container will be a row.

    • withCrossAxis

      public static @NonNull LinearLayout.Builder withCrossAxis(@NonNull Axis crossAxis)
      Returns a LinearLayout.Builder that can be used to make a layout container that can be used to create a layout container that places the specified widgets side by side, perpendicular to the specified axis. If crossAxis is Axis.VERTICAL the container will be a row, if crossAxis is Axis.HORIZONTAL the container will be a column.

    • withWeight

      public static @Nullable Widget withWeight(double weight, @Nullable Widget w)
      This only takes effect is justifyContent is set to LinearLayout.JustifyContent.STRETCH. In case of other JustifyContent values, the weights will be ignored.

      Similar to flex-grow in CSS or Flexible.flex in Flutter or weight in Android.

      Parameters:
      weight - must be a positive and finite number
      w - if null, this method will return null

    • withAlignChildren

      public @NonNull LinearLayout withAlignChildren(LinearLayout.AlignChildren crossAxisAlignment)
      Makes a new LinearLayout where every item will be aligned as specified in the parameter along the cross axis.

      If the specified alignment is not LinearLayout.AlignChildren.STRETCH, and a child had cross axis alignment set with Align, this alignment will overwrite it.

    • reversedIf

      public @NonNull LinearLayout reversedIf(boolean reverse)
      If the parameter is true, returns a LinearLayout that displays the children in the reverse order of the children's current order (with the same gap, direction, etc.). If the parameter is false, returns a LinearLayout that behaves exactly the same as this LinearLayout.
